pr_title: Fix embedded subwindow drag in single window mode
pr_body:
<!--
Pull requests should always be made for the `master` branch first, as that's
where development happens and the source of all future stable release branches.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed.

Do not create a pull request for stable branches unless the change is already
available in the `master` branch and it cannot be easily cherry-picked.
Alternatively, if the change is only relevant for that branch (e.g. rendering
fixes for the 3.2 branch).
-->
Fixes #47244

The problem was that it was using the position of the last dragged sub window. So, I added a new drag state `SUB_WINDOW_DRAG_START`. When the drag starts, the `drag_from` and `drag_pos` variables are set to the initial position of the sub window and the mouse.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6378569/111965647-32250c80-8ab3-11eb-98f5-72acc3a04b77.mp4
pr_comments:
Why it needs new enum `SUB_WINDOW_DRAG_START` ?

I just change only (on original)
```cpp
gui.subwindow_drag_pos = sw.window->get_position();
```
to
```cpp
gui.subwindow_drag_pos = gui.subwindow_focused->get_position();
```

It seems to work for me too.

> Why it needs new enum `SUB_WINDOW_DRAG_START` ?
> 
> I just change only (on original)
> 
> ```c++
> gui.subwindow_drag_pos = sw.window->get_position();
> ```
> 
> to
> 
> ```c++
> gui.subwindow_drag_pos = gui.subwindow_focused->get_position();
> ```
> 
> It seems to work for me too.

Much cleaner! Didn't know I could get the the currently focused from window from `gui`. Updating PR with the change.

Could you squash the changes to a single commit? It appears your newer commit reverts some changes you did on a previous one.

Edit: I want to note I haven't tested it yet.

Edit 2: Tested. Seems to work correctly. It also seems to fix the crash I found while reproducing the issue. I'll wait to look deeper into the code and do further testing.
This appears to have been superseded by #53419. Please comment if that's not the case.

issue_context.title: Embedded subwindows (single window mode) dialogs draw in the incorrect position
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
-->

**Godot version: 47cf9985ebf2799d9718fa1a2ca96f2f70c6d212**
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->


**OS/device including version:Linux**
<!-- Specify GPU model, drivers, and the backend (GLES2, GLES3, Vulkan) if graphics-related. -->


**Issue description:**
<!-- What happened, and what was expected. -->
When in single window mode, floating windows (popup, floating docks, etc.) get re-positioned to the last moved window.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Enable single window mode
2. Make two docks floating (scene tree, inspector, filesystem, etc.)
3. Move one dock
4. Move another dock


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6378569/111925817-8efad580-8a67-11eb-9d3e-ba13fcbb0c75.mp4



**Minimal reproduction project: N/A**
<!-- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue. Drag and drop a zip archive to upload it. -->
comments: Should we even allow detaching docks while in single-window mode in the first place? I can't see a whole lot of use cases for detaching docks if you can't move them outside the editor window.

Disabling floating docks might be a good idea, but we shouldn't disable that feature in single window mode just to fix this bug. There are other ways to replicate this bug, for example, viewing the generated shader code in the visual shader editor suffers from the same issue. 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6378569/111932437-a7282000-8a7a-11eb-9bb9-d78b5660cfd4.mp4

It appears the situation has changed. The initial impression is that the popup menus get the correct position, however something is up with them, I'm not sure what (Edit: I now know what, they are responsive according to the "current window", if that makes sense). Also, I managed to crash Godot, so yay!

Edit: These appear to be the steps to crash:

- Open the generated shader code window as depicted in the video above.
- Open one of the main window menus (e.g. Scene)
- Try to drag the generated shader code window (note: without closing the menu first).
I think this is the same as #50949 and #51445, both of which were fixed by #53419. Are you still having this issue on the current `master` @pcvonz?
Assuming fixed, please comment if you can still reproduce it in 4.0 alpha 1.
